title: Closing again after Reopen voids the old record and adds a new one
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Make sure the Internal Work Orders setting is on in Settings > Work Orders.
  • Make sure AccountingHub is enabled for the organization and the test location has no QuickBooks Online connection.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer A, flagged as an Internal customer.
  • Have a new internal work order for this test, work order 1, for internal customer A, closed, with one approved line with one stock part picked from inventory at a cost of $40.00 each, quantity 2.
custom_steps:
1. Open work order 1.
  2. Open the Finance tab.
  3. Open the invoice menu on the Finance tab.
  4. Click "Reopen Work Order".
  5. Click Reopen Work Order in the window.
  6. Click Close Work Order in the work order header.
  7. Click Close Work Order in the confirmation.
  8. Open Accounting > Sales > Invoices.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Work order 1 opens.

Step 2:

  • The document shows.

Step 3:

  • The menu offers "Reopen Work Order".

Step 4:

  • The window opens.

Step 5:

  • The status reads "Complete".

Step 6:

  • The confirmation opens.

Step 7:

  • The work order is Closed again.

Step 8:

  • The first record is Void; a new Closed record carries work order 1's number.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.0 final (9 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11761 (Story 4, Reopen a closed internal or no-charge work order), story SV-11765 (Story 8, AccountingHub, the closed work order and its parts cost)

  • S8-R4: “At Reopen, the hub posts the reversing entry linked through the existing Reversal links, and the record of S8-R1 is voided as a reversed invoice is today.”
  • S4-R4: “Closing again (Story 3) posts the final numbers as a new entry with the new posting date.”
